headline_seed: Trump says Secret Service and the military wanted him off Air Force One in Turkey due to threat - AP News

consensus_facts: On July 8, 2026, President Donald Trump departed the NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey, and was reportedly secretly transferred off Air Force One via an airport catering truck/container to a separate military aircraft (a C-32A, a military Boeing 757), with the original Air Force One flying as a decoy carrying press and some White House staff.
The plane switch was first reported by The Washington Post on Monday (Aug. 10), and subsequently reported by The New York Times; the reported reason was an Iranian assassination threat.
Trump flew on the alternate military aircraft from Turkey to RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk, England.

On Tuesday, Aug. 11, 2026, speaking to reporters at Joint Base Andrews after returning from Ohio, Trump confirmed the switch and attributed the decision to the Secret Service and the military, saying 'I go by Secret Service and the military' and that 'they wanted me to do it, so I do it.'
Trump downplayed knowledge of a specific threat, saying he receives many threats and did not ask much about it.
Neither the Secret Service nor the White House confirmed or denied the specifics; the White House said only that it uses every tool available to protect the president.

disagreements.topic: Which passengers/officials were on which plane

positions.ABC News: Reports (citing sources) that Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent were on the decoy Air Force One, while Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth flew with Trump on the other plane; all three were aware of the switch.
positions.Associated Press: AP photo caption places Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth watching as Trump switched planes at RAF Mildenhall, consistent with Hegseth being present, but AP does not name the plane assignments of Rubio or Bessent.

disagreements.topic: Who Trump said was at greater risk

positions.ABC News: Headlines and reports Trump saying he was at 'greater risk' on the secret flight than the decoy Air Force One.
positions.USA Today: Reports Trump saying the plane he flew on was at greater risk because 'that would be the plan... they would be more likely to go for.'

disagreements.topic: Nature and source of the threat

positions.USA Today: Reports (attributing to NYT and WSJ) that U.S. officials feared Iranian proxy forces attacking Trump's aircraft; the threat was relayed by Israel and involved shoulder-fired missiles targeting Air Force One.
positions.BBC News: States the exact nature of the perceived threat remains unclear and that the Secret Service has not commented.
positions.Associated Press: Characterizes it broadly as an 'Iranian assassination threat' without specifying method or intelligence source.

positions.USA Today: Describes a multi-plane sequence: a Qatar-gifted jet to Turkey, boarding the powder-blue older Air Force One, secret transfer to a third military jet to England, then believed switch back to the Qatari 747-B for the flight to Andrews.
positions.BBC News: Describes a switch from Air Force One to a C-32A that flew to RAF Mildenhall, without detailing the subsequent leg or a third aircraft.

framing_analysis.Associated Press: Two AP items in the dossier are essentially photo-caption-driven wire dispatches. Both lead by attributing the core claim to The Washington Post ('The Washington Post reports...'), keeping AP at arm's length. Heavy on tarmac/catering-truck imagery and the mechanics of the switch; light on the threat's substance. Neutral, sourcing-forward phrasing; frames Tuesday's remarks as Trump 'confirming' the prior WaPo report.
framing_analysis.The New York Times: Headline-only in this dossier. Frames the event as Trump having 'secretly used a military jet to leave Turkey amid threats from Iran' — emphasis on secrecy and the Iran threat. No body text available to assess lead/burial choices.
framing_analysis.BBC News: Takes the widest analytical lens, framing the episode as one instance of a longstanding Secret Service 'shell game.' Leads with historical precedent (Clinton 2000, Bush 2003 Baghdad, Biden 2023 Ukraine) and expert voices (Kessler, McDonald, Eckloff, Polymeropoulos) to normalize the tactic while stressing this case was a 'different level.' Emphasizes the unresolved question of a government 'duty to warn' unwitting decoy passengers. De-emphasizes Trump's own political framing.
framing_analysis.Reuters: Headline-only in this dossier. Frames it factually via the catering-truck mechanism and Iran threat, with the cautious qualifier 'reports say.' No body text to assess further.
framing_analysis.ABC News: Leads with Trump's attribution of the decision to the Secret Service and the military and his claim of being at 'greater risk' than the decoy plane. Advances the story with sourced detail on which Cabinet members were on which plane. Highlights Trump brushing off knowledge of a specific threat ('I get a lot of threats'). Frames around Trump's words and internal decision-making.
framing_analysis.USA Today: Most detailed body text. Leads with Trump's 'I go by Secret Service' quote and the catering-container mechanics. Adds the most surrounding context: the multi-plane sequence, the Qatari-gifted jet, Trump's 'number one on the kill list for Iran' quote from the summit, the WSJ-sourced shoulder-fired-missile detail, and broader Iran-conflict backdrop (June peace deal, its collapse, renewed strikes on Tehran, Strait of Hormuz). Frames the ruse within Trump's self-presentation as a heavily targeted, 'consequential' president.

primary_source_alignment: No primary source (Secret Service statement, White House confirmation, intelligence document, or full transcript of Trump's tarmac remarks) was located for this story. All threat-specific claims trace back to reporting by The Washington Post, The New York Times, and The Wall Street Journal, none of which appear as full primary documents in the dossier.

The underlying originating report (Washington Post, Aug. 10) is not present in the dossier; every full-text outlet here explicitly attributes the core narrative to that report rather than to independent confirmation.
missing_context: No outlet in the dossier provides the actual Washington Post report as a source document — it is the load-bearing origin of the entire story but is only referenced secondhand.

The specific nature, credibility, and intelligence provenance of the Iranian threat is unverified; USA Today attributes shoulder-fired-missile and Israel-relay details to NYT/WSJ, but the BBC states the threat's nature 'remains unclear.'
Neither the Secret Service nor the White House has officially confirmed the plane switch on the record; the story rests substantially on anonymous sources and Trump's own after-the-fact remarks.

No outlet clarifies whether the unwitting decoy passengers (press pool, Cabinet members not in the know) were ever formally notified or whether a 'duty to warn' obligation applied — the BBC raises the question but leaves it open.
There is no independent corroboration of the exact catering-truck/container mechanism beyond the reports attributing it to WaPo/NYT and unnamed sources.
The dossier contains no on-the-record Iranian government response or denial regarding an alleged assassination plot.
USA Today's account of a third aircraft and a switch back to the Qatari 747-B is single-sourced within the dossier and not corroborated by the other full-text outlets.
brief.suggested_post_type_reason: Multiple outlets reported the same July 8 event but with materially different framings — AP as a cautious wire attribution, BBC as a historical 'shell game' analysis, ABC and USA Today foregrounding Trump's own words and threat details — while the load-bearing primary source (the Washington Post report) and any official confirmation are absent, making this a coverage-and-sourcing story rather than a settled straight REPORT.
